slot.brief: Four orders of electron gain enthalpy (including Cl vs F and S vs O anomalies) are given; pick the incorrect one.

stem: Using $X>Y$ to mean that $X$ has a more negative electron gain enthalpy than $Y$, which order is incorrect?

verdicts.working: More-negative electron gain enthalpy: Cl > F > Br > I and S > Se > Te > O. Thus (A), (B), and (D) are correct; (C) incorrectly places F above Cl.

working:
More negative electron gain enthalpy: $\text{Cl}>\text{F}$, $\text{S}>\text{Se}>\text{Te}>\text{O}$, and $\text{Cl}>\text{Br}>\text{I}>\text{O}$. Hence the order with $\text{F}>\text{Cl}$ is incorrect.

Independent check: More-negative electron gain enthalpy: Cl > F > Br > I and S > Se > Te > O. Thus (A), (B), and (D) are correct; (C) incorrectly places F above Cl.
solution: Electron gain enthalpy is more negative for Cl than F because F’s compact $2p$ shell increases electron–electron repulsion. The order is $\text{Cl}>\text{F}>\text{Br}>\text{I}$; hence the order placing F above Cl is incorrect.
